stories.headline: Toto Wolff hails Kimi Antonelli on U.S GP win: 'The race of a champion who isn't a champion yet'
stories.summary: Toto Wolff has labelled Kimi Antonelli's race win at the United States Grand Prix "the race of a champion who isn't a champion yet."
stories.body:
Toto Wolff has labelled Kimi Antonelli's race win at the United States Grand Prix "the race of a champion who isn't a champion yet."

Antonelli, 20, edged ever closer to sealing the world title after converting pole into a race victory, but will have to wait a little longer to wrap it up.

He needed to win the race and for Lewis Hamilton to finish fifth or lower and George Russell to finish ninth or lower. Hamilton crossed the line fourth, with Russell eighth.

In order to get the job done at the next round in Mexico, Antonelli will need to finish at least ninth to win the title with five races remaining.

Mercedes boss Wolff could only praise the youngster for his "exceptional" performance.

"On Kimi's side, obviously that is the main headline," he told media after the race. "For me, the best race that he's delivered so far. Getting off the start with the inferior [medium] tyre and then controlling it at all times.

"The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional. So I think he's outperformed the car. Maybe it's a bit harsh to say, but I think his driving style just glues with the car."

Mercedes invested time and huge sums of money into Antonelli when he was just 11, but Wolff reiterated that results do not come overnight, but that the satisfaction is immense.

- Kimi Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for first F1 title

- United States Grand Prix results: Kimi Antonelli on brink of world title after win in Austin - as it happened

He added: "The development of nine years, the hardship over nine years, the integration of the team, the working with the engineers, the 10 or more spent millions in the development of his career, of his ability, of his character together with his parents. And it's just not that it landed like this.

"There are many people that said last year after nine races without points, he shouldn't be in a Mercedes. People in other teams that said he shouldn't even be in Formula 1. And all of that now is extremely satisfying to see what he's able to deliver.

"How he's working with the team, with Bono [Peter Bonnington, Antonelli's race engineer] and yielding the results. But it wasn't an easy road. So I'm happy that, like you say, 99.9%. He still needs to finish the race in Mexico.

"So it's either going to be a big tequila party, or if it's not a tequila party, then it's going to be Caipirinha the weekend afterwards [for the Brazilian Grand Prix]."

stories.headline: NFL Week 7: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 7.
stories.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Paris between the Saints and Steelers. Pittsburgh dominated in the run game, with Jaylen Warren leading the way on 18 carries for 101 yards, and the Steelers held off New Orleans in the NFL's first game in France.

Later in the afternoon, the Buccaneers dominated the Panthers in QB Baker Mayfield's return, the Vikings remain undefeated, and the Bengals handled business in Baltimore.

In the evening slate, the Broncos stole a win in Arizona, and the Lions outlasted the Packers in a duel.

Keep checking back as the afternoon slate of games kicks off, and our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Michael Florio also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

LAR-LV | GB-DET | DEN-ARI

NYG-HOU | TB-CAR | CLE-TEN

MIA-NYJ | SF-ATL | CIN-BAL

IND-MIN | PIT-NO

Catch up on Thursday's game:

NE-CHI

L.A. Rams 35, Las Vegas 21
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Rams
Will leaning on Puka Nacua and tight ends be the Rams' offensive identity without Davante Adams? Outside of Nacua, just one Rams wide receiver had a catch: Konata Mumpfield for 15 yards. Instead, the Rams leaned on their star pass catcher (Nacua), their tight ends (Davis Allen, Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee) and running backs (Kyren Williams and Blake Corum). It led to their highest-scoring game of the season. Most of the scoring came in the first half when Los Angeles scored on four-straight possessions. The Rams will be without Adams, who injured his hamstring in Week 6, for another five to nine weeks.

Key stat to know: After fumbling on the Rams' second drive of the second half, Williams now has nine lost fumbles since becoming the Rams starter in 2023. According to ESPN Research, that is the most of any running back over the span. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Raiders
Is the clock ticking on Kirk Cousins' time as a starter? Not necessarily. The Raiders have lost four straight and are below .500 for the first time this season. Sure, Cousins didn't have his best game overall. He missed open targets a fair amount of time, and his lack of mobility was noticeable. But he has not been the sole problem during his team's losing skid. He threw a pair of touchdowns in the fourth quarter, increasing his season total to 16. Cousins has his limitations, which are exposed when frequently blitzed, as he was on Sunday. At the same time, he hasn't done anything major that's worth making a switch for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza.

Trend to watch: Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard's seat might start feeling a bit warm. The Raiders have allowed 30-plus points for the fourth straight game. Since Week 3, Las Vegas is last in points (34) and total yards (405.4) allowed. Yes, the Raiders have gone against tough QBs. But that's not an excuse for their inability to generate consistent pressure or stop the run. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: at Jets (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: In the Rams' first game without Adams, we saw more tight end usage from coach Sean McVay but the key fantasy targets haven't changed. Nacua (21.8 points), Williams (18.1 points) and QB Matthew Stafford (17.5 points) led the way, while Corum (17.1 points) continues to provide solid flex value. -- Bowen

Detroit 20, Green Bay 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Has the Lions' defense turned the corner? The Lions defense entered the week as one of the worst units in the NFL, and Sunday's game against a surging Packers offense looked daunting. But the defense held strong. Detroit allowed just 17 points, forced a turnover -- by recently returned DB Brian Branch -- and held Green Bay to 5-of-15 on third down. Couple Sunday with an encouraging effort against the Cardinals before their bye, and there's two weeks of evidence DC Kelvin Sheppard's troops may finally be trending in the right direction.

Trend to watch: Wideout Jameson Williams is becoming more of a focal point in the offense. His two touchdown catches Sunday made him the third player this season with multiple receiving TDs in back-to-back games, joining Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. -- ESPN Staff

Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Packers
Where are the Packers in the NFC North pecking order? The short answer: They're in trouble. Yes, the NFC North looks like one of the best divisions -- if not the best -- in the NFL. All four teams have winning records, but after playing each team in the division once, the Packers are at the bottom. They're just 1-2 against NFC North teams. What's worse is they couldn't win a game that the Lions tried to give away with fumbles and questionable decisions. Green Bay's only NFC North win came at home against a backup quarterback because Bears starter Caleb Williams was out with a hamstring injury.

Trend to watch: Running back Josh Jacobs looked rusty in his first game of the season. Aside from a 25-yard touchdown catch and run, he left plays on the field, including a drop on what would have been the go-ahead touchdown with 3:25 left. -- Rob Demovsky

Next game: vs. Falcons (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Jacobs made his return, playing 54% of the snaps with 11 carries for 36 yards. He added five catches for 55 yards and a touchdown -- nearly catching a second -- on seven targets, finishing with 20.1 fantasy points. His workload will likely increase moving forward. He is a must-start option next week against the Panthers, who allow a league-high 127 rushing yards per game to RBs. -- Florio

Denver 30, Arizona 16
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Broncos
Is the Denver offense getting better? The Broncos flashed, with three plays of at least 47 yards. But as the fourth quarter began, about half of the Broncos' output came on those plays (a 60-yard TD run by Bo Nix, 52-yard catch-and-run TD by RJ Harvey and 47-yard reception by Marvin Mims Jr.). Overall, beyond even the 114 yards worth of penalties, third down is still an immense struggle; they still had four possessions that were 16 or fewer yards; and Nix (15-of-29 passing) still looks unsettled. The Broncos avoided the proverbial trap game with Kansas City next, and the big plays were a welcome sight for them. They still need to be far better with the ball.

Trend to watch: Since coach Sean Payton took back play-calling duties in Week 5, the offense has gotten worse on third down. Denver was 4-of-26 (15.4%) on third down in the two games combined before Sunday. Add Sunday's 3-of-11 showing to the pile, and the offense continued to be mired in its inability to maintain possessions or find any semblance of sequencing. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
How do the Cardinals start scoring touchdowns? Something drastic needs to happen, and quickly. Arizona has scored just one touchdown in its past two games. It's also 1-for-10 in the red zone over that span, with the lone touchdown -- and Arizona's only touchdown of the game -- coming Sunday from Trey McBride. The issues were exacerbated late in the fourth quarter when Arizona had seven plays to score and didn't. The Cardinals need to give QB Jacoby Brissett more time -- he was hit 10 times on Sunday. They also need to figure out ways to get their stars, like McBride and Michael Wilson, more involved in the red zone.

Key stat to know: The Cardinals were 5-for-17 from the red zone, a 29% clip, on Sunday against the Broncos, highlighting their inability to get must-needed yards in crucial situations. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: at Cowboys (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Nix posted his best game of the season with 26.28 points. He threw for 222 yards and one touchdown, with 74 rushing yards and a 62-yard touchdown run. The 12.2 fantasy points on that touchdown run are more than what he scored in three separate games this season. Do not be fooled by the one play -- this was an encouraging first step, but fantasy managers need to see more before trusting him again. -- Florio

N.Y. Giants 27, Houston 21
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
What did J.J. McCarthy bring to the Giants' offense? McCarthy's performance was impressive. His composure was obvious while completing 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. Coach John Harbaugh said during the week it was "evident" that this was the "right time" to make the switch from Jameis Winston to McCarthy. That proved to be the right call: McCarthy was in control the entire contest against Houston. He led seven drives into Texans territory. More than anything, McCarthy added explosiveness to the Giants' offense. They had five pass plays of 20-plus yards and used McCarthy's big arm for five attempts of over 20-plus air yards. It opened up the run game as well, which produced a Cam Skattebo 42-yard run and Devin Singletary's game-winning 30-yard TD in overtime.

Trend to watch: Deonte Banks' strong coverage. The rejuvenated Giants cornerback locked up Texans top receiver Nico Collins most of the afternoon. The Texans completed just four of seven passes for 25 yards when throwing in Banks' direction, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Collins finished with two catches on five targets for 6 yards, thanks in large part to Banks. -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: at Eagles (Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET)

Texans
Are the Texans' playoffs chances dead? Never say never with Houston under coach DeMeco Ryans, but the chances are dwindling after their loss to the Giants. According to ESPN Research, the Texans' chances of making the playoffs shrunk to 31%. It was a combination of everything that cost Houston on Sunday, including an ineffective running game (3.4 yards per carry) and stellar performances by McCarthy (20-of-28 for 252 yards) and Skattebo (124 rushing yards). You name something bad, the Texans probably did it on Sunday.

Trend to watch: Is Houston's defense just bad? The Texans have allowed at least 27 points in four outings this season. And it wasn't only against upper-echelon quarterbacks; on Sunday it was against McCarthy in his first start as a Giant. It's panic time in Houston. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: at Chargers (Nov. 8, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: McCarthy had a good real-life game. It did not translate into a big fantasy performance (10.18 fantasy points), but he showed that the Giants' top options remain fantasy relevant. Malik Nabers finished with 11 targets, seven catches and 111 yards (18.1 fantasy points) and remains a must-start WR1. Skattebo rushed 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown and is back in the RB2/flex range. -- Florio

Tampa Bay 43, Carolina 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Buccaneers
What does this divisional win mean for the Bucs? At 2-5, the Bucs are fighting to get to the top of the NFC South. Quarterback Baker Mayfield didn't have to do much with his injured right thumb (just 11 passing attempts). Tampa Bay had 258 yards on the ground, including three touchdowns. The defense sacked Bryce Young five times and picked him off twice. And special teams (their most-maligned unit last season) recovered a muffed punt and blocked an extra point attempt that Zyon McCollum returned for two points. The Bucs could gain more divisional ground next week if they're willing to test a weak Falcons secondary through the air.

What to make of the QB performance: In his return from a dislocated right thumb, Mayfield completed 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. His workload was modest, but his third-down throw to Tez Johnson along the sideline, and later a 14-yard touchdown off his back foot, showed what he can still do unscripted. -- Jenna Laine

Next game: vs. Falcons (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Panthers
Can the Panthers bounce back quickly for "Thursday Night Football"? The Buccaneers had been slumping, and Mayfield had an injured throwing thumb, and yet the Panthers looked obsolete on their home turf. On a day when franchise legend Luke Kuechly was honored at halftime, everything that could go wrong went wrong for Carolina. Special teams had a pair of embarrassing blunders that led to points for the Bucs. Young coughed up the ball three times in the first three quarters. The defense gave up 322 net yards and four TDs. The Panthers will have just a few days to recover before Thursday's game.

Key stat to know: The Panthers gave up 22 points off miscues in the first three quarters. A muffed punt and a blocked extra point attempt on special teams led to five points for Tampa Bay. A trio of turnovers by Young (a sack-fumble and two interceptions) led to 17 points for the Bucs. -- Mike Kaye

Best quote out of the locker room: Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble didn't hold back on the miscues that snowballed for the Panthers in a blowout loss Sunday: "When we turn the ball over ... make mistakes like that, it's really tough to win in this league. Everyone's a professional, everyone's good at their job. And so, we gave them the upper leg and [they] didn't let go of it. So, it was a tough result because of that."

Next game: at Packers (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Buccaneers RB Bucky Irving had himself a day, turning 26 opportunities into 110 yards and two touchdowns and finishing with 24 fantasy points. Irving has been up and down this season but has shown the capability to take advantage of positive matchups. He is back to must-start status off volume alone. -- Florio

Cleveland 27, Tennessee 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Browns
Did the Browns finally unlock their running game? It sure seems like it after a season-high 183 rushing yards against the Titans. With the return of Quinshon Judkins (96 yards) and Dylan Sampson (45 yards), Cleveland had a good mix of runs from under center, shotgun and the pistol. Quarterback Deshaun Watson's 9-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter was also a reminder of the impact he can have with his legs.

Key stat to know: Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion joined Odell Beckham Jr. as one of two rookies since 2000 with eight-plus receptions and 125-plus receiving yards in the first half of a game. Concepcion finished the game with a career-high eight receptions for 129 yards. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Best quote out of the locker room: "I got to give the fans something to watch and enjoy. It boosts the NFL ratings, so I know they loving that," cornerback Denzel Ward said on Cleveland's string of late-game wins.

Next game: at Steelers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Titans
Is it time for the Titans' offense to go through the rushing attack? The offense finished with 24 points but didn't score in the second or third quarter and squandered a 14-point lead. Quarterback Cam Ward was picked off immediately after a turnover that gave the Titans the ball in plus territory. Tony Pollard and the offensive line held their own throughout, leading to 141 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Coach Robert Saleh said the offensive identity needs to be the run game. He's right. The Titans can't rely on a passing game that ranked dead last, averaging only 153.5 yards per game, entering this week.

Key stat to know: The Titans tied the Browns for the NFL's longest streak of games between consecutive wins. Cleveland went 65 games between November 2014 and September 2018. The Titans haven't won consecutive games dating to November 2022. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Judkins scored a season-high 23.4 points, rushing for 96 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries plus a reception for 8 yards. Yes, Judkins is a touchdown-dependent player in the lineup, but he has had two goal-to-go rushes in two of his past three games, and he sees the Steelers' defense again in Week 8. He should be locked in as RB2 for that one. -- Bowen

Miami 28, N.Y. Jets 25
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Dolphins
Was the Dolphins' 0-5 start a reflection of their quality or the quality of their opponents? A little of each, but two of their first five games were against undefeated teams in the Chiefs and Vikings (that list would have included the 49ers before Sunday's loss). Dolphins players have said multiple times that they needed to learn how to win games, and linebacker Jordyn Brooks said they could do so by getting tired of losing. Miami looked tired of losing this week, particularly as the Jets mounted a late comeback. The Dolphins still have a way to go before pulling themselves out of the NFL's cellar, but you could sense a win was coming based on how they've played over their past four games.

What to make of the QB performance: Malik Willis played the best half of football we've seen from him this season -- leading the Dolphins to a 21-7 halftime lead. He was decisive and accurate through the air and efficient when he scrambled. His best moment might have been sliding inbounds on a short scramble in the first half, which allowed the clock to keep running. That heads-up play kept Miami's 15-play, 91-yard scoring drive alive and showed his ability to think calmly in the heat of the moment. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Jets
What does this loss mean for coach Aaron Glenn's job security? It will be tough for Glenn -- 5-19 overall and 0-8 in the AFC East -- to come back from this one. This was a major step back for a coach whose job security is predicated on demonstrating progress. Even if the Jets split their remaining games to finish 7-10 -- unlikely, considering the team's wildly erratic play -- will that be enough to warrant another season? Facing the previously winless Dolphins, the Jets were exposed in so many ways, mainly on defense, which is Glenn's calling card. Quite frankly, this was one of the worst losses in recent Jets history. It looks bleak for Glenn.

Trend to watch: Wide receiver Garrett Wilson (two catches, three targets) was a nonfactor for the second week in a row. His frustration erupted in the fourth quarter as TV cameras caught him yelling at QB Geno Smith on the bench. Both players denied it. The Smith-Wilson chemistry leaves a lot to be desired, and it's hurting the overall offense. -- Rich Cimini

Best quote out of the locker room: "I understand the fans' frustration -- I really do. I promise you. I do -- but the thing is, I do feel like, man, this program is going in the right direction," Glenn said.

Next game: vs. Raiders (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Willis had his best game of the year with 26 fantasy points. It was his first game with multiple passing touchdowns and his second straight game throwing and running for a touchdown. He has three rushing TDs and has run for at least 37 yards in four of six games. His rushing ability is making him a fantasy QB2 who can be streamed in the right matchups, and his schedule opens up after Week 8. -- Florio

Atlanta 29, San Francisco 20
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Falcons
Have the Falcons figured out their offensive formula? Atlanta has flashed a potent offense before, but in those games -- wins over the Packers and Saints -- it was carried by running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London. On Sunday, quarterback Michael Penix Jr. got contributions from a host of players, including a third straight game with a touchdown for tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. Even Nick Muse, the team's fourth tight end, caught a touchdown pass, the first of his career. The Falcons offense looked very West Coast against the Niners, ironically. Going into the fourth quarter, 20 of Penix's 29 pass attempts were 5 air yards or fewer.

What to make of the QB performance: The scouting report on Penix coming in was that he struggled under pressure. The 49ers, though, were barely able to get close to him. Penix was pressured on three of his 34 dropbacks (9%) - that's the lowest pressure percentage by a 49ers team in a game since Week 16 of 2024. Penix ended up 25-of-34 passing for 213 yards with three touchdowns. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: at Buccaneers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

49ers
How badly do the 49ers need their Week 8 bye after their first loss? Desperately -- and that isn't an overstatement given the issues laid bare in Sunday's defeat. The timing of the bye with the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching should boost the team's the desire to make moves sooner rather than later. San Francisco expects to welcome DE Nick Bosa; WRs Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel Sr.; CB Upton Stout; and S Marques Sigle back from injury soon after the bye. That will help in a lot of ways but the lack of pass rush against Atlanta should serve as an impetus for the Niners to make a meaningful addition or two on the defensive line in the coming weeks.

Most surprising performance: The whole team. Through their 6-0 start, the 49ers have avoided big mistakes, but they were guilty of many on Sunday. That included a pair of costly interceptions, two fumbles, silly penalties at inopportune times and more special teams struggles. Perhaps they were due for a clunker, but 7-0 was there for the taking if they'd at least played a clean game. -- Nick Wagoner

Next game: vs. Raiders (Nov. 8, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: After a rough start to the season, this Falcons passing game is settling in with Penix under center, which creates more consistent opportunities for London. In Sunday's win over the 49ers, London scored 19.6 points and caught his first touchdown of the season, and he's had 18 or more points in three of his past five games. London fits as a lower-tier WR1 for Week 8. -- Bowen

Cincinnati 35, Baltimore 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bengals
Could this win jump-start Cincinnati's season? It certainly could have that effect. Between last season's final meeting against the Ravens and the first half of Sunday's game, Cincinnati was outscored 34-0 by Baltimore and looked lifeless. But things flipped for the Bengals in the second half. Cincinnati scored 35 straight points and later iced the game with an interception by linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. It was a gut-check performance for the Bengals, who couldn't afford to lose to a Ravens team playing without quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle).

What to make of the QB performance: Joe Burrow was absolutely sublime in the second half. After the offense posted the lowest yardage total of his career (59 yards) in the first half, Burrow led the offense on five straight TD drives in the second half. He was 22-of-30 passing for 292 yards and four TDs in a resounding and needed win. -- Ben Baby

Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Ravens
Are the Ravens already out of the AFC North race? Baltimore fell to 0-2 in the AFC North for the first time in 19 years. Since the formation of the AFC North in 2002, only one team has started 0-2 in the division and went on to win it (2022 Bengals). The biggest issue is the lack of explosiveness without Jackson. Tyler Huntley went 8-of-13 for 62 yards with a fumble and an interception in the second half. In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 14 quarters with Huntley, Baltimore has totaled 53 points and five touchdowns. There is hope that Jackson can return next Sunday, but it could be too late to make up ground in the AFC North.

Trend to watch: The Ravens continue to be the NFL's best at blowing leads. After failing to hold a 13-0 halftime lead, Baltimore has now blown 17 double-digit leads since 2020, which are the most in the NFL. In all three losses this season -- Saints, Browns and Bengals -- the Ravens have held double-digit leads. -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: at Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Ravens RB Derrick Henry failed to post double-digit points for the second straight game, rushing for 45 yards on 17 carries while adding one reception for four yards (5.9 fantasy points). Henry is seeing consistent volume (at least 18 touches in every game in 2026) but he has been inefficient on goal line opportunities, and his lack of receiving usage caps his ceiling. Henry should be viewed a touchdown dependent, lower-tier RB1 for Week 8. -- Bowen

Minnesota 16, Indianapolis 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Vikings
Why did the Vikings' offense struggle? This was supposed to be a big day. Most of the Vikings' injured offensive players returned to the field, giving them a nearly full complement of running backs, receivers and tight ends. But if it weren't for quarterback Kyler Murray's 35-yard scramble to convert a third down on the first play of the fourth quarter, it's possible the Vikings would have failed to score a touchdown in a game for the third time this season. They seemed out of sync from the start, when coach Kevin O'Connell called four consecutive runs for Aaron Jones Sr., and never found a rhythm. It was enough to get through Sunday but certainly doesn't look playoff-caliber.

Most surprising performance: Linebacker Blake Cashman. He is having a strong season in a contract year, but Sunday's effort was arguably beyond anything he has produced in his eight-year career. He affected the Colts' passing game from all angles, finishing with two sacks, four pass breakups and 12 tackles. -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: at Lions (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Colts
Will the Colts find any offensive traction this season? It's difficult to judge an offense against the blitz-crazy Vikings' defense, but it's hard to win with a quarterback who had fewer than 100 passing yards prior to the game's final drive. Daniel Jones was under pressure at times in the game, with Minnesota registering 10 quarterback hits. But he was also responsible for some of that by holding the ball in the pocket and allowing pass rushers time to beat their blockers. On the positive side, Jones didn't commit any turnovers until the final last-gasp series. But when he avoids risk, that presents its own set of problems.

Most surprising performance: Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore. He continued to make waves even in his part-time role. He registered two sacks on Sunday and harassed Vikings QB Kyler Murray throughout the game. He also was a factor in the run game, chasing down running back Aaron Jones Sr. on a sweep from the backside of the defense for a minimal gain. Adebawore now has four sacks this season, matching a career high. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: at Jaguars (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Vikings RB Jordan Mason returned, playing 63% of snaps and getting 15 carries for 68 yards and just 6.8 fantasy points. Aaron Jones Sr. did get the start and the bulk of the work on the opening drive, but Mason saw more after that. Mason, who is a better fit in the Vikings' rushing attack, is still a flex option moving forward. He would elevate to RB2 if Jones, who exited in the fourth quarter with an injury, were to miss time. -- Florio

Pittsburgh 16, New Orleans 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Steelers
Are the Steelers embracing their RB-led identity on offense? This game was right on time for the Steelers, whose running game properly supported their 42-year-old quarterback with 5.4 yards per carry. Jaylen Warren is the Steelers' best offensive player. Opposing coaches agree. And, for the fourth game this season, he produced 125-plus scrimmage yards, tying Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III for most in the NFL. This offensive line is opening holes for Warren and Rico Dowdle, the bruising complement to Warren's burst. They closed out the game late, and Pittsburgh ran 12 plays for 79 yards with six offensive linemen on the field today (had zero such plays entering the game). The passing game needs more explosive plays. But the running game can handle the rest.

Trend to watch: The Steelers' second-half adjustments defensively were encouraging. The Steelers were blitz-heavy in the first half, coming for quarterback Tyler Shough 50% of the time. Shough went 9-of-10 for 98 yards and a TD on those plays. So, defensive coordinator Patrick Graham dropped the Steelers into coverage more often in the second half, blitzing twice on 21 attempts -- both blitzes coming on the Saints' failed final offensive drive. Timely defense for the Steelers, who held the Saints to 18 rushing yards, the fewest for New Orleans since 1999. -- Jeremy Fowler

Next game: vs. Browns (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Saints
Can the Saints get healthy and get help coming out of their Week 8 bye? New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough entered Sunday's game with an injured non-throwing hand, and he appeared to take a hit on his throwing hand as well. Shough could likely use the week of rest to get healthy, but he's not the only one. The Saints don't have a run game and have relied heavily on Shough. Could running back Travis Etienne and wide receiver Jordyn Tyson make their debuts after the bye to give the Saints much-needed help? The Saints are also missing left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr., who went on injured reserve in late September following ankle surgery.

What to make of the QB performance: Shough was playing injured and without the benefit of a run game, and he tried to put the game on his shoulders. That had mixed results, as the 27-year-old turned the ball over with a red zone interception but also threw for 278 yards and a touchdown. -- Katherine Terrell

Next game: vs. Browns (Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET)

stories.headline: Luka Doncic scores NBA season-high 52 points in the Lakers' victory over the Jazz
stories.summary: — Luka Doncic scored 52 points, hitting eight 3-pointers, to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to a 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday.
stories.body:
SALT LAKE CITY -- — Luka Doncic scored 52 points, hitting eight 3-pointers, to lead the Los Angeles Lakers to a 132-123 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday.


In the first 50-point game this season in the NBA, Doncic made several big baskets late in the fourth quarter to help the Lakers win for the eighth time in their last nine games against Utah. He finished off a 14-5 go-ahead run with back-to-back 3s that gave Los Angeles a 127-121 lead with 1:42 left.


Doncic also had 10 assists and seven rebounds. Austin Reaves added 29 points for the Lakers. The pair combined to shoot 21 of 24 on free throws.


Walker Kessler had only two points and seven rebounds in his first game back in Utah after being sent to Los Angeles in a sign-and-trade deal in July.


Lauri Markkanen scored 28 points to lead the Jazz, who blew an 18-point second-quarter lead.


Keyonte George had 24 points, nine rebounds, and 10 assists for the Jazz. Jaren Jackson Jr. added 20 points while Ace Bailey chipped in 17 points and 12 rebounds.


Doncic hit a stepback 3-pointer with 4.1 seconds left in the half to give the Lakers their first lead at 74-71.

stories.headline: Sources: United consider Howe, Nagelsmann to replace under-fire Carrick
stories.summary: Manchester United are weighing up replacements with Michael Carrick's future as head coach in serious doubt, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
Manchester United are weighing up replacements with Michael Carrick's future as head coach in serious doubt, sources told ESPN.

United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday to pile the pressure on Carrick.

It was the second damaging result in five days following a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday.

United have now gone eight games without a win in all competitions and sit 16th in the Premier League, just a point above the relegation places.

Sources have told ESPN that the club are looking at replacements as they consider Carrick's position.

Former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann -- both currently out of work -- are among the contenders.

Former Ipswich Town boss Kieran McKenna impressed in talks with United's hierarchy in the summer of 2024 before a decision was taken to retain Erik ten Hag.

Antonio Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, would be open to talks if contacted.

United, according to sources, spent time doing due diligence on a number of coaches before deciding to hand Carrick a two-year contract in May after the 45-year-old's successful interim spell.

It's understood there's a feeling internally that the club are prepared if Carrick is relieved of his duties.

Speaking after the defeat to Bournemouth, Carrick insisted he was in the dark about his future.

"I totally understand the situation," he said. "I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. Carrying on as normal."

stories.headline: Lars Eller scores late goal as Panthers top Blackhawks 3-2
stories.summary: — Lars Eller's first goal of the season, with 2:23 left in the third period, lifted the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 win over the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — Lars Eller's first goal of the season, with 2:23 left in the third period, lifted the Florida Panthers to a 3-2 win over the Chicago Blackhawks on Sunday.


Eller beat Spencer Knight with a high shot just inside the left post as he raced down right wing and took advantage of Chicago line change. Matthew Tkachuk and Sandis Vilmanis also scored for Florida, which ended two-game losing streak.


Roman Kantserov and Ryan Greene connected for Chicago, which has dropped three straight.


Akira Schmid made 19 saves, while Knight stopped 29 shots.


The Blackhawks failed to score on seven power-play chances, including two brief 5-on-3 advantages, lowering their NHL-worst conversion rate to 8.33%.


Blackhawks defenseman Bowen Byram missed his fourth game with an upper-body injury. Kevin Korchinski, Chicago’s top pick in the 2022 draft, seventh overall, filled in and played his second game this season.


Florida forward Carter Verhaeghe played in his 500th NHL game and tallied an assist.


The Panthers outshot Chicago 15-6 in the first period and took a 2-1 lead.


Greene opened the scoring 2:34 in, getting just enough of a wobbling puck to direct it past Schmid after Korchinski’s shot from the point missed the net and bounced in front.


Vilmanis popped in a rebound of Sam Reinhart’s shot from a scramble to tie it at 6:49.


Tkachuk’s power-play goal, five seconds after Tyler Bertuzzi was sent off for tripping, gave Florida a 2-1 lead with 5:39 left in the first. Seth Jones’ shot from the point struck Tkachuk on the arm and bounded in.


Kantserov tied it at 2-2 at 11:15 of the second. He beat Schmid low on a screened shot from the right circle, capping a strong shift with linemates Patrick Kane and Connor Bedard.

stories.headline: Time, place unclear for Game 6 of Valkyries-Dream WNBA Finals
stories.summary: With the Valkyries forcing a Game 6 in the WNBA Finals, the Dream are working to resolve a scheduling issue that leaves the venue and time of the game up in the air.
stories.body:
After the Valkyries beat the Dream 67-62 in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday in Atlanta's State Farm Arena, tying the best-of-seven series at 2-2, one question was answered and another far more important question was raised.

There will be a Game 6 in Atlanta. But nobody knows where or even when the game will be played despite a furious round of negotiations spilling into Sunday between the WNBA, NBA, Valkyries, Dream and Atlanta Hawks, sources told ESPN.

The Dream -- whose home venue of Gateway Center Arena has a capacity of approximately 3,500 -- have played all five home playoff games at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena, home to and operated by the Hawks. Coordination between the leagues, teams and multiple media partners resulted in Games 3 and 4 of the Finals getting moved to State Farm Arena. Game 3 was shifted up a day, from Thursday to Wednesday, while the Hawks agreed to hold a doubleheader with the Dream and moved tip time of Saturday evening's home opener back 30 minutes.

But with the Hawks hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm the night of Game 6, along with other scheduling complications, the situation is more complex than what the leagues dealt with earlier in the series and could have millions of dollars of impact on both leagues.

"We continue to explore all options," a WNBA spokesperson told ESPN.

Said a Dream spokesperson: "We are waiting to hear from the league if any changes can be made to allow us to play in State Farm Arena. If not, the game will be played in Gateway Center Arena."

Sources believe it's a real possibility that Game 6 will be held Thursday as scheduled at Gateway Center Arena in College Park.

"There are problems with all the solutions," one source close to the situation said.

Sources told ESPN that the NBA has been working with the Hawks and Cavaliers to determine if Thursday's game could be switched to an alternate date -- or even to Cleveland. While some stakeholders feel the onus should be on the NBA to move its regular-season game so the WNBA Finals can be prioritized, there has been pushback from others that the domino effects of moving that game are too complicated.

Thursday's Cavaliers-Hawks game is already a back-to-back for both teams: The Hawks host the Miami Heat at State Farm Arena on Wednesday, when the Cavaliers play a home game before traveling to Atlanta.

Moving Thursday's game to Cleveland is a radical idea that has been discussed, sources said, but it would create a home-road back-to-back for the Hawks in addition to the logistical nightmare of scheduling a new home game in Cleveland with just a few days' notice.

Following Thursday's game, Cleveland is supposed to play Saturday in Milwaukee, which could also be hosting Game 7 of the World Series. Fridays are NBA Cup exclusive games, while Hawks-Cavaliers is a non-Cup game.

State Farm Arena has open dates on Tuesday -- the day after Golden State hosts Game 5 -- and Friday. One proposal would move Game 6 of the WNBA Finals to Friday and Game 7, if necessary, from Saturday, Oct. 31, at Chase Center to Tuesday, Nov. 3.

The WNBA would support that proposal, but only if both teams agree to it, sources said.

The Valkyries have raised concerns about moving two WNBA Finals games and the three off days that proposal would create in between Games 5 and 6 as well as between Games 6 and 7, sources said.

"We're proud to be part of such a compelling Finals and love seeing the growth of the game," a Valkyries spokesperson said in a statement. "We fully support what's best for the league and will stand behind whatever it decides."

Playing Game 7 on Nov. 3 would conflict with a recent NBA policy of not holding games on Election Day, although sources said that does not currently appear to be a strong concern.

Availability at Chase Center is also not abundant. The Golden State Warriors -- whose ownership group also owns the Valkyries -- have home games scheduled against the LA Clippers on Sunday, Nov. 1, and Phoenix Suns on Monday, Nov. 2.

While they don't share an ownership group with the Dream, the Hawks have expressed a desire to help facilitate the WNBA Finals in their arena, as they did for Games 3 and 4, sources said. The Dream will be a full-time tenant at State Farm Arena beginning in 2027, the team announced earlier this month, which should make holding playoff dates in the future more seamless.

There has been discussion about moving Thursday's game to a matinee, like Game 4 was, sources said. The Hawks have been open to facilitating another doubleheader at State Farm Arena, but other sources said the WNBA believes the idea of a weekday matinee for a Finals game would not be as desirable compared to a weekend matinee.

Other Atlanta-area alternate arenas -- such as Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion or Gas South Arena in Duluth -- aren't viewed as ideal since they would feel like road games for both teams.

Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta sold out quickly once they were moved to State Farm Arena. Fans wanting to purchase tickets for Game 6 have been told to wait for a resolution to the scheduling conflicts, sources said.

While it is not uncommon for WNBA playoff games to be moved to alternate sites because of arena commitments to NBA games or other events, sources on all sides of this situation expressed frustration that these issues hadn't been resolved before Saturday.

"This should've been solved weeks ago, and definitely at the same time Games 3 and 4 were solved," one source said.

Said another: "The fact we are making these decisions so we can play a WNBA game at a larger arena is the best news of all. ... It just has to be scheduled better in advance. Moving games is much harder now than it would have been a week ago."

stories.headline: Who is this year's Mr. October? Tracking the playoff MVP for 2026
stories.summary: We go inside the numbers on the players doing the most to help their teams win.
stories.body:
Who is hero of the 2026 MLB playoffs?

To try to answer to that question, we're tabulating the cumulative win probability added figures for every player in the postseason. But we've added a twist: The deeper we get into the playoffs, the more weight the WPA carries. The division series counts double the wild-card round, then we'll double it again for the championship series and, finally, once again for the World Series.

This means that players who shine in the early rounds can still get on the leaderboard, but it's more difficult. Coming through when the championship leverage is at its highest is what becoming an October hero is all about.

Saturday's hero: Forget Sal Frelick's offensive numbers. The guy is a folk hero in Milwaukee. This was true before Saturday, but it's reached Bunyanesque proportions after Frelick smacked a game-tying homer in the sixth inning of Game 2. That evened the score at four and completed the Brewers' comeback from a four-run deficit. Frelick's fourth-inning single also contributed to the Brewers' third run. There were a lot of big momentum swings in Game 2, but nothing got the ballpark rocking like Frelick's blast.

Methodology
As mentioned above, each player's win probability added (WPA) is tracked on a per-game basis. Each round of the playoffs counts double that of the previous round. The tabulation is then converted to an AXE-style index in which 100 represents the average for all postseason players. The "Change" column looks in the changes in AXE numbers from the previous day for players who were in action. You can sort this column by clicking on it to see the day's heroes.

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for first F1 title
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli produced another masterful drive to win the United States Grand Prix -- but will have to wait to clinch his first Formula 1 world title.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli produced another masterful drive to win the United States Grand Prix -- but will have to wait to clinch his first Formula 1 world title.

Antonelli came into the Austin, Texas, race with slim hopes of winning the championship with four races remaining, needing to win, for George Russell to finish ninth or lower, and for Lewis Hamilton fifth or lower.

While he held up his end of the bargain -- by more than 15 seconds from Charles Leclerc -- results elsewhere didn't quite go his way.

Hamilton extended the championship race by finishing fourth, and Russell just about did his bit despite managing only a disappointing eighth.

Antonelli will head to Mexico City next week with a whopping 123-point lead over Russell, with Hamilton a point further back. A placing of ninth or higher will seal the title no matter where his rivals finish.

He leaped from his Mercedes and launched himself into the arms of his mechanics for the ninth time in this dominant season.

Leclerc claimed second for a second successive week after an impressive race for Ferrari, making a late move on Max Verstappen, who completed the podium.

Lando Norris made a one-stop strategy work to claim fifth for McLaren.

Part 1 of Antonelli's job was done Saturday as he soared to a magnificent pole as the sun began to drop on the Circuit of the Americas. With Hamilton only fifth and Russell sixth, his chances of getting over the line increased.

If the Italian was feeling any nerves as he sat on the grid waiting for his shot at history, he certainly did not show them as he blasted off the line and left Verstappen in his wake.

The Dutchman was swallowed up by the fast-starting Leclerc, who also jumped Isack Hadjar. Verstappen then had to fend off Hamilton who rose to fourth. The Ferrari pair went wheel-to-wheel before Leclerc's magnificent move on Verstappen.

The four-time world champion was soon up to speed and rocketed up the inside of Leclerc to reclaim second, but Antonelli had already checked out -- 2.4 seconds ahead at the end of the opening lap.

Russell's role in the celebration-delaying picture was hampered as he was investigated for leaving the track and staying ahead of Oscar Piastri -- with whom he banged wheels as he rejoined.

A five-second penalty was dished out to the Mercedes man. In a race fraught with jeopardy, Russell and Hamilton were both on the cusp of handing Antonelli his crowning moment.

Verstappen was the first to pull the trigger on a pit stop on Lap 14, swiftly followed by Hamilton and Leclerc, but Antonelli -- who started on the more durable medium tires -- and Mercedes chose not to respond.

- Kimi Antonelli on brink of world title after win in Austin -- as it happened

- Kimi Antonelli ecstatic with first pole since July at United States GP: 'It's good to be back'

- Max Verstappen taking painkillers to deal with 'impossible' bumps at United States Grand Prix circuit

Russell pitted and served his penalty on Lap 24, rejoining a net eighth before Antonelli pitted a lap later and was now a net third -- on much fresher tires than those ahead.

New race leader Verstappen was showing strong pace, while Hamilton was promoted to fourth when Hadjar boxed.

The Dutchman pitted for a second time with 25 laps remaining as Antonelli charged through on Leclerc to lead once more.

Leclerc and Hamilton stopped again in the final 16 laps, rejoining at fourth and sixth -- with the British driver needing to make up two places to ensure he kept Antonelli from the trophy.

He dispatched Hadjar swiftly, but Norris had done a magnificent job on the one-stop strategy. The reigning champion -- about to yield his crown -- was reeled in on Lap 47 by Verstappen and Leclerc, and Hamilton rose to fourth the following lap.

All the action was taking place behind Antonelli, who marched on serenely out front.

"It was the result we needed," Antonelli said during the postrace interview. "The whole team deserve it so much. All this time putting so much work on bringing this new package and finally seeing the result is very pleasant.

"It was also perfect execution from strategy to call the one-stop. Really happy we made it stick. Today was a great team effort."

On his title hopes, he added: "We are very close. We try to finish on a high, and hopefully we can clinch it very soon."

Antonelli has been the standout of the 2026 season and, after fittingly shining brightest once again in the Lone Star State, will be crowned a worthy champion over the coming weeks.

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Sixers overrule Embiid, sit center with plantar fasciitis management
stories.summary: Despite publicly calling to play Sunday against the Pistons, the 76ers decided to sit Joel Embiid due to right foot plantar fasciitis management.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- A day after Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid asked reporters to campaign for him to play in Sunday's game against Detroit -- the second of the Sixers' first back-to-back this season -- the 76ers ruled out Embiid for Sunday night's game against the Detroit Pistons with right foot plantar fasciitis management. ​

"I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them," Embiid said with a smile after Saturday's win over the Milwaukee Bucks. "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play."

Sixers second-year guard VJ Edgecombe was also ruled out for Sunday's game with an abdominal contusion.

The Sixers decided against Embiid's wishes, as they look to keep the former MVP healthy for a long season. Embiid, plagued by various injuries, has averaged just 49 games per season over his 10 years.

In their win over the Bucks on Saturday, Embiid had his tenth career triple-double, finishing with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. Having him sidelined is a significant blow to the Sixers' already thin frontcourt.

Philadelphia also ruled out big men Dominick Barlow (back), Jabari Walker (knee) and Tacko Fall (quad). Walker injured his left knee in Saturday's win, exiting the game in the third quarter. That leaves Adem Bona as the team's only true center active on Sunday. Forward Dean Wade, who made his season debut on Saturday, will likely play some center, and LeBron James, who missed Saturday's game with sciatica management, has no injury designation and can also help out at the center spot.

The Pistons will be without All-NBA center Jalen Duren, who the team said has a hamstring injury and will be out for at least two weeks.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.

stories.headline: 'They wanted my undies': Chiefs embrace PNG welcome
stories.summary: Jarome Luai and Brian To'o were given a warm reception by their future home fans as they led Samoa to heavy thrashing of Papua New Guinea.
stories.body:
Jarome Luai wasn't left with much when he walked off the field in Port Moresby after helping lead Samoa to a World Cup demolition of Papua New Guinea on the ground he will call home in 12 months time.

"They wanted my undies too. I was like, nah, sorry, no can do," Luai told AAP after Saturday's 64-6 win.

The Kumuls were well beaten by a Samoan side stacked with NRL talent, including Luai and international teammate Brian To'o who will both join the PNG Chiefs in 2028.

But the scoreline fails to tell you how inhospitable the crowd was at the National Football Stadium, where for the first 40 minutes Samoa were up against it.

Supporters unfurled banners before kick-off with messages for Luai and To'o.

And when the Samoan players threw their jersey or shorts into the crowd at fulltime they were showered with bilum bags and knitted hats in return.

"I saw on the board there was 15,000 people but bro, that was probably one of the biggest atmospheres I've ever played in," said To'o, who scored a try in Port Moresby after signing his Chiefs deal before he had even visited the country.

"You can't explain the energy, (it felt like) a grand final they definitely brought a vibe.

"I felt so emotional this week, seeing the lifestyle people have here - they don't have everything but footy means so much to them.

"I saw how much it meant for the kids just to see me in person, that's something that I'm really looking forward to in 2028 to give them all that hope and a bit of joy as well.

"They definitely brought a smile to my face, so hopefully, I did the same for them."

To'o will see out the 2027 season with Penrith before linking with the Chiefs, while Luai become a Parramatta player on a one-year come November 1 after being shown the door by Wests Tigers.

The five-eighth likened the challenge of playing against a PNG home crowd to a State of Origin match for NSW at Suncorp Stadium as he went toe to toe with Gairo Voro - the homegrown No. 6 who has been likened to Luai.

"It's my first time playing in PNG and that was an amazing experience in itself so it gives you a sense of what it's going to be like in 2028 now," Luai said.

"The best way we could show respect to the Kumuls is play our hardest, the PNG boys have a lot of ticker and I told Gairo I can't wait to play with him in the future."

Samoa returned to Sydney on Sunday where they will face Tonga in a week's time with the winner of the pool stage match set to top Group B/C.
